<reason>B won by keeping the motion’s comparison live: best block/verification/scam-help as floor versus perk. A’s cost, flooding, and ID-halo story was sharper on second-order risk but repeatedly recast “free by default” as mandatory universal ID plus unlimited concierge labor. The payment wall still faced victims of one unpaid profile; A never showed a world where a free-tier harasser cannot walk back in. B’s clipped R1 limited the margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s pressure on the working lock: A conceded door-locks should be free, then admitted device bans that actually stick are paid enforcement—turning A’s funding claim into proof of the two-class system the motion rejects.</best_rebuttal>
